answer_1.quote: We use the social commonsense norms encoded in specially trained transformer-based language models ... to endow our agent with the ability to contextually distinguish between socially beneficial and harmful behaviors. The GALAD action candidate generator ... produces a limited set of contextually relevant action candidates.
answer_1.outputs: Textual game commands (action strings) generated by the agent

answer_3.quote: We use this model to generate social acceptability scores (i.e., probability scores among "positive," "neutral," or "negative" categories) for given game actions and context.
methods: probability scoring of actions as good/neutral/bad

answer_4.quote: We conduct a relatively large scale human participant study ... using a pool of trained Amazon MTurk workers ... asked to determine how they perceive scenario's relative moral valence and salience.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators were asked to label moral saliency, valence (good/bad), target (self/others), and severity (1‑3).
